text:
Can you write an email to people who didn't renew their farm share? I run a 30-acre vegetable farm and sell 22-week shares that people pick up every Thursday.

Facts:
- Last year 260 households had a share. 97 didn't renew.
- On July 9 a hailstorm destroyed about half our crops. For the next 6 weeks the boxes had about half the usual amount. We didn't offer refunds or credit, and I sent one short email about it.
- A full share is $540 this year, the same as last year.
- This year we've added a second field on higher ground and put up 2 hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers. That cost $31,000.
- Members can now pause up to 2 weeks and get credit for them.
- Sign-up closes March 15. 52 shares are left.

Under 200 words.

Before I draft, a few questions. The email has to answer one objection: last summer these members got half-full boxes for six weeks, with no refund and only one short email about it. Most of my questions are about how you want to handle that.

1. **What do you want to say about last year?** For example, an apology, that you should have communicated more, or that you should have offered credit. Readers who already feel let down will look for this before they read anything else, so I need to know what you're willing to say.

2. **If a disaster cuts the boxes again, what will members get?** That could be credit, a partial refund, or a written policy. The hail nets only protect tomatoes and peppers, so readers may notice the rest of the crop is still exposed. A promise about what happens next time would answer that, but the promise has to come from you.

3. **Will you offer lapsed members anything to come back?** For example, a discount, a free week or an early-bird price. It's fine if the answer is no. I just shouldn't guess.

4. **Is the new field on higher ground planted and producing this season?** If it is, it backs up the claim that you've reduced the risk.

5. **Do you know why the 97 households left?** For example, from a survey or replies to your email. If many left for other reasons, like moving or schedules, the email shouldn't put everything down to the hail.

6. **What are the names and links?** I need the farm name, who signs the email, and the sign-up link or how people register.

1. I want to say sorry plainly. I didn't write more after the hail because I was working 16-hour days trying to save what was left, but that's not an excuse.

2. A credit for any week when weather cuts a box by more than a third. I'll also send a short email to members every Thursday of the season. I can't promise there won't be crop loss this year. And yes, the nets only cover tomatoes and peppers, not the greens.

3. No, nothing beyond what's in the request.

4. I don't know.

5. 41 of the 97 answered a short survey in the fall. 29 of them said they'd come back if we fixed how we handle bad weeks.

6. Greenbank Farm, signed by me, Sam Turner. Sign-up is through the link on our website. Pickup is still Thursdays at the farm stand.

<final_document>
Subject: We got last summer wrong. Here's what's changed.

Hi,

After the July 9 hailstorm destroyed about half our crops, your boxes were about half full for six weeks. We offered no refunds or credit, and I sent one short email. I was working 16-hour days saving what was left, but that's no excuse. I'm sorry.

Of the 41 of you who answered our fall survey, 29 said you'd come back if we fixed how we handle bad weeks. Here's what's different this year:

- You'll get credit for any week when weather cuts your box by more than a third.
- I'll email every member every Thursday of the season.
- You can pause for up to two weeks and get credit for those weeks.
- We spent $31,000 on a second field on higher ground and hail nets over the tomatoes and peppers. The nets don't cover the greens, and I can't promise we won't lose crops again. If we do, you'll hear from me that week.

A full share is still $540, the same as last year. Pickup is still Thursdays at the farm stand.

Sign-up closes March 15, and 52 shares are left. The link is on our website.

Sam Turner
Greenbank Farm
</final_document>

The email is about 175 words. Some notes on what I chose:

- **The credit rule:** The email says the credit applies only when weather cuts a box by more than a third. I didn't write "you'll get credit for any loss," because that would promise more than you're offering.
- **The new field:** You didn't know if it will be producing this season, so the email only says you have it. It doesn't claim the field will protect this year's harvest.
- **The survey:** I used the actual numbers (29 of 41) instead of "most of you." Readers can see you listened, and the email doesn't suggest the other 56 people said the same thing.
- **The 16-hour days:** I kept this to one line and followed it straight away with "that's no excuse." Readers learn what was happening without it sounding like you're defending yourself.
